browser_cache_ttl.description:
Controls how long the browser is allowed to cache the content.
  - The CDN will add a Cache-Control header to the response sent to end-users with the configured cache TTL.
  - Set the value of the browser cache TTL in seconds.

cache_behavior.description: Controls whether content should be cached by the CDN, possible values: `BYPASS`, `CACHE`

cookies.description: Set of cookies to include in the cache key

country.description: Include the client country in the cache key

device_type.description: Include the client device type (mobile/desktop) in the cache key

headers.description: Set of headers to include in the cache key

params.description:
Set of query string params to include or exclude in the cache key.
  - Required when `type` is `include` or `exclude`.
  - Must be omitted when `type` is `all` or `none`.

type.description:
Controls which query string params are part of the cache key.
  - `include` / `exclude`: use the params listed in `params`.
  - `all`: include every query string param (no `params` allowed).
  - `none`: ignore all query string params (no `params` allowed).

cache_ttl.description: Set the value of the edge cache TTL in seconds

cached_methods.description: Controls the list of HTTP methods whose responses the CDN will cache

  - Required when mode is `specific`, must be empty otherwise.

  - Required when mode is `specific`, must be empty otherwise.
  - Valid values: `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`

origins.description:

  - Required when mode is `specific`, must be empty otherwise.

values.description:
List of exposed headers 
  - Required when mode is `specific`, must be empty otherwise.

deny_access.description:
Controls whether the CDN should deny access to requests that meet the behavior condition.
  - When enabled, the CDN will return a 403 Forbidden response.

ip.description: IP address or CIDR block to deny

deny_access_by_ip.description: Controls whether the CDN should deny access to a specific set of IP addresses.

end_date.description: End of the interval as a Unix timestamp (UTC).

start_date.description: Start of the interval as a Unix timestamp (UTC).

date_time_window.description: A fixed UTC time interval during which access is denied.

duration.description: Duration of the deny access window (numeric value, paired with `duration_units`).

repeat_period.description: Interval at which the deny access rule repeats (numeric value, paired with `repeat_period_units`).

start_date.description: Start of the first interval as a Unix timestamp (UTC).

time_periodic.description: A recurring time interval during which access is denied.

deny_access_by_time.description:
Controls whether the CDN should deny access during a specific time period.
  - The time period can be either a fixed interval (`date_time_window`) or a recurring one (`time_periodic`). 
  -

follow_redirects.description:
This action enables the CDN to follow a redirect response from the origin.
  - If the origin responds with a redirect, the CDN will follow it and return the response to the end user.
  - **Limitations**:
    - The host in the `Location` header must be defined as an origin in the service.
    - The scheme in the `Location` header must be HTTPS.

allowed_headers.description:
Value for the `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` header.
  - List of request headers the browser is allowed to send in the actual request.

allowed_methods.description:
Value for the `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` header.
  - Valid values: `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS` 
  -

max_age.description:
Value for the `Access-Control-Max-Age` header in seconds.
  - Controls how long the browser may cache the preflight response.

generate_preflight_response.description:
Controls how the CDN should respond to a preflight request.
  - The CDN can respond to a preflight request without forwarding it to the origin.
  - You can configure the headers to include in the preflight response. 
  -

generate_response.description: Return a custom response page for specific status code(s)

use_origin_host.description: Use the origin domain name as the Host header for the origin. Must be set to `true`.

host_header.description:
Override the Host header sent to the origin.
  - Set `header_value` to a specific hostname, or set `use_origin_host = true` to use the origin's own hostname.
  - The two fields are mutually exclusive. 
  -

origin_cache_control.description:
Controls whether the CDN should honor the Cache-Control header sent by the origin.
  - By default, origin Cache-Control headers are not honored by the CDN.

  - Set `values` to add/override a header, or set `delete = true` to remove it.

stale_ttl.description:
This action sets the time duration the CDN can serve expired content from the cache
  - If the content is expired and there is a problem fetching it from the origin, the CDN can serve stale content for the specified duration.
   - Set the cache TTL value in seconds.

cache_ttl.description: Value of browser cache TTL - in seconds

status_code.description: Status code to apply the configuratoin for (1xx,2xx,.. can be used for ranges)

status_code_browser_cache.description: Define browser cache configuration for status code(s)

cache_behavior.description: Cache behavior for this status code. Valid values: `BYPASS`, `CACHE`

status_codes_ttl.description: Cache TTL configuration per status code

log_destination.description:
Name of the log destination to stream logs to.
  - The destination must be configured in the service's `log_destinations` block.

log_sampling_rate.description:
Percentage of requests whose logs should be streamed (1–100).
  - Use `100` to stream all logs, or a lower value to sample.

stream_logs.description:
Stream CDN access logs to a configured logging destination (e.g., an S3 bucket).
  - All logs are delivered in a unified format, regardless of which CDN provider generated them.
  - See IO River Documentation for details on how to configure a destination.

true_client_ip.description:
Controls whether the CDN should add a `True-Client-IP` header when forwarding the request to the origin.
  - When enabled, the header will contain the real IP address of the end user.

destination.description: The new path, which can be either a static string or a regex.

source.description: The source request path, which can be either a static string or a regex.

url_rewrites.description:
This action enables rewriting the request path.
  - The destination path can be a static string or can be derived from a regular expression.
  - This action takes place before the content is retrieved from the cache.
  - Example: The following removes the static prefix from the request path:     Source `/static/(.*)`, Destination `/$1` 
  -

url_signing.description: Controls whether the CDN should verify the URL signature before allowing access to the content.

viewer_protocol.description:
Controls how the CDN should respond to HTTP requests.
  - The CDN can either accept both HTTP and HTTPS, redirect HTTP to HTTPS, or restrict access to HTTPS only.
  - If HTTPS-only is selected, the CDN will respond with a 403 status code to HTTP requests.
  - Allowed viewer protocol - can be one of the following: `HTTPS_ONLY`, `HTTP_AND_HTTPS`, `REDIRECT_HTTP_TO_HTTPS`.

field.description: Field to match against. Valid values: `http.request.domain`, `http.request.path`, `http.request.method`, `http.request.header`, `http.response.status_code`, `http.response.header`, `client.geo.country`, `client.device.is_mobile`, `http.request.query_param`, `client.ip`

field_key.description: Key within the field (required for header and query_param fields)

value.description: Single-value shorthand for `values = ["..."]`. Mutually exclusive with `values`.

values.description:
List of values to match against.
  - For `ip_match`/`not_ip_match` provide CIDR blocks or individual IPs (e.g. `["10.0.0.0/8", "1.2.3.4"]`).
  - For `exists`/`does_not_exist` set an empty list (`[]`).
  - For all other operators provide one or more string values. 
  -  - Mutually exclusive with `value`.

and.description: List of conditions that must ALL match (AND group)

or.description: List of AND groups (OR of ANDs expression)

condition.description:
Full match condition (OR-of-ANDs expression).
  - Mutually exclusive with `path_pattern`. 
  -

path_pattern.description:
Simple path pattern shorthand (e.g. '/api/*').
  - Mutually exclusive with `condition`.
  - Internally expanded to a single `http.request.path` / `match` condition.

action_token_threshold.description: Bot score above which an action token is required. Range `0.0`–1.0`. Default `0.5`.

challenge_threshold.description: Bot score above which a challenge is issued. Range `0.0`–1.0`. Default `0.5`.

web_key.description:
reCAPTCHA Site Key. Add this key to your front-end code to enable action-level bot mitigation.
  - This key is issued by IORiver and is required for bot management to function.
  - If you do not have a key, contact IORiver support to obtain one.
  -

bot_management.description:
Bot-management keys and challenge thresholds.
  - `web_key` is issued by IORiver.
  - Both thresholds are floats in `[0.0, 1.0]` and default to `0.5`.
  -

action.description: Action when rule matches. Valid values: `block`, `log`, `allow`, `bypass_managed`, `ignore`, `challenge`, `interactive_challenge`

field.description:
Request field to evaluate.
  - Plain fields (no `field_key` needed):
    - `http.request.method` (HTTP verb)
    - `http.request.path` (URL path, e.g. `/api/users`)
    - `http.request.uri_raw` (full raw URI including query string)
    - `http.request.body` (request body text)
    - `client.ip.address` (client IPv4/IPv6 — use `ip_match`/`not_ip_match`)
    - `client.ip.asn` (autonomous system number)
    - `client.geo.country` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code)
    - `bot.advanced.score` (IO River bot score 0-100 — supports `lt`/`le`/`gt`/`ge`)
    - `client.ja3` (JA3 TLS fingerprint hash)
    - `client.ja4` (JA4 TLS fingerprint hash)
  - Collection fields (require `field_key`):
    - `http.request.header`
    - `http.request.cookie`
    - `http.request.query_param`
    - `http.request.json_param` 
  -

field_key.description:
Name of the specific header, cookie, query parameter, or JSON body field to inspect.
  - **Required** when `field` is one of `http.request.header`, `http.request.cookie`, `http.request.query_param`, or `http.request.json_param`.
  - For example: `field_key = "User-Agent"` when `field = "http.request.header"`. 
  -

operator.description:
Match operator to apply.
  - **String:**
     - `eq` (exact match),
    - `ne` (not equal),
    - `begins_with` / `not_begins_with`,
    - `ends_with` / `not_ends_with`,
    - `contains` / `not_contains` (substring),
    - `contains_word` / `not_contains_word` (word-boundary match),
    - `regex` / `not_regex` (Python-compatible regular expression).
  - **List:**
    - `in` / `not_in` (value is in the supplied list).
  - **IP/CIDR:**
    - `ip_match` / `not_ip_match` (use with `client.ip.address`; supply one or more CIDRs/IPs in `value`).
  - **Existence** (set `value = []`):
    - `exists` / `does_not_exist` (field/header/cookie/param is present or absent).
  - **Numeric** (use with `bot.advanced.score`):
    - `lt`, `le`, `gt`, `ge`. 
  -

value.description: Single-value shorthand for `values = ["..."]`. Mutually exclusive with `values`.

values.description:
List of values to match against.
  - For `ip_match`/`not_ip_match` provide CIDR blocks or individual IPs (e.g. `["10.0.0.0/8", "1.2.3.4"]`).
  - For `exists`/`does_not_exist` set an empty list (`[]`).
  - For all other operators provide one or more string values. 
  -  - Mutually exclusive with `value`.

and.description: List of conditions that must ALL match for this OR group to be satisfied.

or.description:
OR-of-ANDs match expression.
  - The rule matches when **at least one** OR group matches.
  - Each OR group contains one or more `and` conditions that must **all** match simultaneously. 
  -

value.description: Value associated with the ignore type

ignore_params.description: Parameters for the 'ignore' action (required when action = ignore)

custom_rules.description:
Ordered list of custom rules, evaluated **before** the WAF engine.
  - Rules are evaluated first-to-last.
  - **Actions:**
    - `block` (return 403 immediately, do not evaluate further rules or WAF engine),
    - `log` (allow the request, and add to sampled logs),
    - `bypass_managed` (allow + skip managed ruleset),
    - `allow` (skip remaining rules and WAF engine),
    - `challenge` (automatic Captcha challenge),
    - `interactive_challenge` (always interactive Captcha challenge),
    - `ignore` (instruct WAF engine to ignore a specific parameter — requires `ignore_params`).
  - **Conditions:**
    - Each rule condition uses an OR-of-ANDs expression: the rule fires when at least one OR group matches, and all AND conditions in that group match. 
  -

num_of_requests.description: Number of requests that trigger the rate limit

time_window_seconds.description: Time window in seconds for counting requests

rate_limit.description:
Ordered list of rate limiting rules. 
  - A rule fires when the client IP exceeds `num_of_requests` requests within the `time_window_seconds` sliding window.
  - The client is then subject to the rule's action for `block_duration_seconds`.
  - **Actions:**
    - `block` (drop excess requests),
    - `log` (observe without blocking),
    - `challenge` (automatic Captcha challenge),
    - `interactive_challenge` (always interactive Captcha challenge),
  - **Conditions:**
    - Each rule condition uses an OR-of-ANDs expression: the rule fires when at least one OR group matches, and all AND conditions in that group match. 
  -

high_confidence_action.description: Action for high-confidence matches. Valid values: `block`, `log`

low_confidence_action.description: Action for low-confidence matches. Valid values: `block`, `log`

medium_confidence_action.description: Action for medium-confidence matches. Valid values: `block`, `log`

performance_impact.description: Include rules with performance impact at most: `low`, `medium`, `high`

severity.description: Include rules with severity at least: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`

ips.description: Intrusion Prevention System (IPS - rules-based engine) settings

minimal_num_sources.description: Minimum number of trusted sources required for learning

trusted_sources.description: List of trusted source IP addresses used for learning mode

checkpoint.description: Checkpoint WAF partial configuration. Some settings (e.g. learning mode results) are managed via the UI; the fields here control the active enforcement configuration.

security.description: Security configuration (WAF, custom rules, rate limiting)

account_provider.description: The account provider to be assigned to this service

is_failed.description: An indicator of whether the ServiceProvider is in a failed state

is_unmanaged.description: Is this an unmanaged ServiceProvider, which means that the provider is not managed by IO River and will not be configured automatically. This is a write-only field required during creation of the service provider

name.description: Name of the provider, e.g. Fastly, Cloudflare, etc.

provider_custom_data.description: ServiceProvider custom data in JSON format. This is a write-only field used to pass provider-specific information during creation or update of the service provider

service.description: The id of the service this service provider belongs to

status.description: ServiceProvider status, e.g., Active, Deploying, etc.

status_details.description: ServiceProvider detailed status, providing additional information about the current status of the ServiceProvider

geos.description: List of geos to apply this policy on (leave empty for entire world)

performance_penalty.description: Performance penalty (percentage) for cost based policy

is_commitment_priority.description: Priority for utilizing the service provider’s commitment

priority.description: Service provider pririty for cost based policy

providers.description: List of service provider within this policy

service.description: The id of the service this TrafficPolicy belongs to

provider_keys.description: Keys for each provider to be used by the backend to sign URLs.

service.description: The id of the service this key belongs to
